subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
subtype: Approach: staying calm and not replying in anger [Thinking]
passage: The photo appeared in the class group at twenty to ten: a private one of Pranav, meant for a single friend. His face went hot, then cold. His thumbs were already typing, Who did this??? and worse. He looked at the words, then deleted them. If he fired back, they would screenshot that too, and it would become a fight instead of a wrong done to him. He put the phone face down and breathed until his hands stopped shaking. Then he called his cousin Kunal, who told him, “Don't answer anyone. Go to your mother now.” Pranav walked into the living room. His mother listened, put an arm round him, said, “This is not your fault,” and picked up the phone to call the school's safety lead that night.

qa.q: What did Pranav do with the angry message he typed?
What was Pranav feeling when the photo appeared?
qa.a: Panic and rage: his face went hot, then cold, and his thumbs began typing angry words.

qa.q: What could Pranav do next, and why?
qa.a: Save screenshots with dates and share them with the school, since adults can act on real proof.

qa.q: How does the night look to Pranav's mother?
qa.a: Pranav's mother is shocked and worried but glad he came to her, and phoning the school safety lead the same night gives her something useful to do.

grounding: A teen who sees a private photo shared in a class group decides an angry reply would fuel it and goes to an adult first.
